Performers
Oratorio Chorus (chorus) Documented

Densmore’s catalogue transcription describes Edison 80292-R as ‘Mixed voices with orchestra — Oratorio Chorus’. The orchestra’s identity, conductor and individual players are not credited; Edison is the record company, not a performer.

[1] [2] [3] [4]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The catalogue describes mixed voices with orchestra, but no performing edition, arranger or individual instruments are established. No specific orchestral substitution or match to Handel’s original scoring is inferred from that generic credit.

[1] [3] [4]
Recorded
1916 Documented

May 1916 is the release month, not an established session month. The year-level museum session date is retained.

[1] [2]
Place
Unknown Unknown

No session venue is stated in the consulted museum or archive record.

[1] [2]
Label
Edison Diamond Disc Documented

The current museum catalogue identifies a disc; an early Commons upload comment calling it a cylinder is not followed.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
80292-R; NPS object EDIS 43552 Documented

Released May 1916.

[1] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
4433-A-1-1 (6-1), side R Documented

Museum transcription retained without silently interpreting every suffix as a take number.

[1] [2]
Transfer
National Park Service source; Ogg conversion credited to Commons user Pmx Documented

The NPS is identified as the source, not a named transfer engineer. Commons explicitly credits Pmx for Ogg conversion only.

[2] [3]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is established; upload dates are not used as transfer dates.

Processing
The upstream file is a 96 kbps MP3; Commons supplies an Ogg conversion and an MP3 access derivative. Documented

No de-clicking, equalisation or speed correction is documented. Successive lossy formats limit timbral comparison.

[2] [3]
Composition rights
Handel’s eighteenth-century underlying composition is out of copyright under the ordinary life-plus-70 term. Inferred, not documented

The programme note identifies Handel as 1685–⁠1759; this does not clear a later arrangement.

[5]
Recording rights
United States public domain: Edison 80292-R was first released in May 1916. Documented

Programme rule 2; the museum establishes record and issue month. The upstream archive also carries the historic Creative Commons public-domain dedication URL, not a non-commercial licence. The generic Commons PD-US notice is not used to apply a printed-work cutoff to a sound recording.
